summary: Excerpt from Book 1, part 32, a work of fiction narrated by Marcus, a seventeen-year-old high school student held and interrogated by an authority figure and guards. Marcus protests his innocence, then in a cell replays rebuttals he wishes he had made, and the next day is questioned again by the woman. She says the investigation of him is over for now, but warns him he is a marked man under surveillance, forbids him from ever speaking of what happened, invokes national security and the death penalty for treason in wartime, and tells him to sign papers.
one_line: Marcus, a seventeen-year-old student, is interrogated after a national attack, released under surveillance, and warned to keep silent.
key_facts: The narrator, Marcus, describes himself as a seventeen year old high school student, not a terrorist.
Marcus says the woman has been into his stuff and seen all of it.
The woman tells Marcus that he gets pretty good grades and that she thought he would be smarter than that.
Back in his cell, Marcus replays speeches in his mind, including telling her that he is the patriot and she is the traitor.
The narrator says none of his fine words came back to him the next day, when all he could think of was freedom and his parents.
The woman says that the country has experienced the worst attack ever committed on its soil.
The woman asks how many 9/11s the country must suffer before Marcus is willing to cooperate.
The woman says the details of the investigation are secret and that the authorities will not stop at anything to bring the perpetrators to justice.
Marcus is told that he is a marked man and that he has not been found to be above suspicion.
The woman says, We're only releasing you because we're done questioning you for now.
Marcus is told he will never speak of what happened at the facility to anyone, ever.
The woman states that the death penalty still holds for treason in time of war.
Marcus answers Yes, I mumbled to each warning.
The woman calls Marcus a good boy and pushes papers across the table for him to sign.
